jobs.excerpt: OverviewJoin a team where innovation meets mission.
jobs.description:
Overview

Join a team where innovation meets mission. Our AI, cloud, cyber, and modernization solutions save agencies thousands of hours, safeguard national security, and strengthen health and humanitarian missions worldwide. With 1,700+ team members, 1,500+ AI/data experts, and 100+ prime contracts, we deliver at scale and with purpose.

We’ve been recognized as a Top Workplace by the Washington Post for six straight years and named to the Inc. 5000 Fastest Growing Private Companies 13 of the past 14 years. Credence is a welcoming home for those looking to grow and contribute to positive change. We encourage all employees to expand beyond their boundaries, dive into important world-changing Federal challenges.

Position Summary

The Humanitarian Assistance Support Contract (HASC) brings together exceptional institutional support experience, technical leadership, and an unmatched commitment to US missions. HASC supports the U.S. Department of State’s (DOS) humanitarian assistance, disaster response, and foreign assistance across multiple bureaus. Team Credence, through the HASC, delivers operational and administrative support to provide and coordinate humanitarian assistance and maintain 24/7 response capability.

Credence has an immediate need for the Humanitarian Health Advisor, Ebola Response Consultant who will serve as part of the Disaster Humanitarian and Response (DHR) Bureau’s Technical Quality and Assurance (TQA) Office, within the Health Unit. They will be responsible for working on DHR’s response to the current Ebola disease outbreak in West/Central Africa.

The Consultant will also work with other sectors of the office including protection; water, sanitation, and hygiene (WASH); nutrition; natural hazards and shelter and settlements, to provide a multidisciplinary approach to providing life-saving program to disaster affected populations. S/he will support DHR’s approach to emergency health activities within the team and assist in developing response strategies and provide technical support to humanitarian health programming in the Department of State. The Advisor will receive day-to-day guidance from the Senior Health Advisor. S/he will work in close coordination with other Health Advisors.

Scope:

The Consultant will provide technical advisory services to the TQA Office in support of the Department of State’s humanitarian health programming. In addition, the consultant will support DHR’s coordination with the Bureau of Global Health Security and Diplomacy and other bureaus at State and the interagency, including HHS/ASPR, OGA, and CDC.

Overall, the Consultant is expected to show strong independent initiative and work with minimal supervision and engage with stakeholders in close collaboration with and under the direction of the Senior Health Advisor and Ebola Response Leads. Day-to-day oversight of the position will be provided by the Senior Health Advisor, with formal supervisory and evaluation functions performed by a Credence contract supervisor.

The main roles and responsibilities of the Consultant will be:

  • Advise the Response Lead on appropriate strategies on humanitarian response modalities that best enable Ebola outbreak response activities considering lessons learned from past Ebola outbreaks. Identify critical gaps that facilitate the pillars of response and advise the DHR leadership on these strategies.
  • Liaise directly with technical lead and pillar leads of the response at post, and in DC.
  • Advise the DHR Programs Lead on programming. And advise on when other technical sectors need to provide analysis and technical assistance for the response.
  • Engage with the national health cluster and sub-clusters to understand humanitarian gaps, challenges and response plans; attend regular cluster meetings.
  • Evaluate and document health programming gaps and assess the performance of current DHR awards in responding to these gaps.
  • Coordinate with humanitarian partners to understand humanitarian gaps and challenges in light of the Ebola response and understand the integration of health humanitarian actions and Ebola response actions.
  • Attend pillar meetings to understand technical gaps and how they are exacerbated by humanitarian needs or could be better supported through humanitarian enablers.
  • Serve as a USG humanitarian health sector resource person, assist in strategy development and provide expert technical and organizational leadership in sectoral activity as part of Ebola Response.
  • Advise and support technical and strategic thinking for health activities, interventions, and recommendation discussions. Develop sector strategies, guidance, and recommendations (in coordination with other sectors when required) for disaster and humanitarian response; and provide technical support for DHR staff at Post, and other offices within State.
  • Advise and support discussions on emergency health activities with NGO partners and other Department of State staff working in humanitarian health.
  • Provide technical review of proposals submitted by NGO and UN partners for humanitarian health programs. Apply new developments in the emergency health sector to humanitarian programming.
  • Advise on the coordination, implementation and prioritization of emergency health activities to ensure that efforts in assigned program areas are meeting the needs of affected populations and satisfy the goals and objectives of the response program.
  • As needed, provide technical support to State’s humanitarian nutrition and WASH Teams related to the complementary nature of these interventions to improve health outcomes in humanitarian settings.
  • As needed, serve on DARTs and serve on Washington-based Response Management Teams (RMTs), which provides services and support to DARTs deployed in response to disasters. The duties on RMTs will vary. (DARTs may require immediate (within 24 hours) deployment overseas for an extended period of time.)

Requirements

  • Post Graduate Studies (Master’s degree) plus seven (7) years of experience working in emergency relief and humanitarian assistance, and infectious disease outbreaks. A minimum of three (3) years of relevant experience must be obtained overseas.
  • Recent experience working in a technical capacity for an international nongovernmental organization, public international organization, or USG agency working in humanitarian relief and/or response in health and infectious disease outbreaks.
  • Fluency in critical concepts of emergency/ humanitarian health interventions in humanitarian contexts and ability to develop and guide programming to reflect those standards.
  • Understanding of key health issues related to displaced populations, refugees and other vulnerable populations and ability to represent the humanitarian perspective.
  • Demonstrated ability to interpret strategy; to analyze, develop and present work results; and to monitor and evaluate implementation of programs.
  • Demonstrated flexibility and openness in responding to changing work priorities and environments.
  • Fluency in French and experience in the Democratic Republic of Congo strongly preferred.
  • US citizenship with an Active Secret Clearance required.

Working Conditions and Physical Requirements:

  • This position requires the ability to deploy for international travel assignments for at least one month at a time, as well as occasional domestic travel to Washington, DC.
  • When not travelling, this is a fully remote position within the United States and its territories.
  • Consultant may be requested for additional domestic or international travel up to 21 days.

THE OPPORTUNITY

We’re hiring a Creative Director to bring Cyera’s brand to life across every campaign and every touchpoint where a customer, prospect, or employee meets us. Reporting to the Head of Corporate Marketing, you will be a key strategic leader of Cyera’s brand and a core creative voice on the marketing leadership team.

This is not an execution-only role. We’re looking for a creative leader who pairs strong visual instincts with strong writing, and who treats every campaign as a chance to tell a story people remember. You’ll partner closely with Design Studio, Integrated Marketing, and other functions across marketing to make sure Cyera’s brand shows up with the same craft and clarity everywhere it appears, and you’ll lead a small creative team that you’ll be expected to grow, in capability and in ambition.

RESPONSIBILITIES:

  • Brand storytelling across campaigns. Turn Cyera’s positioning and messaging into campaigns that fuse strong visuals with strong copy. Define and build briefs that serve as a guide to make every campaign feel like one idea, carried consistently across every channel and format.
  • Creative direction for key touchpoints. Set the creative bar for the moments that matter most: launches, events, the website, sales collateral, social, and executive communications. Make sure the brand feels like one brand, wherever someone meets it.
  • Partnership with Design Studio. Work hand in hand with Design Studio to turn creative concepts into finished work. Bring clear direction, sharp feedback, and a point of view that raises the level of what gets made.
  • Partnership with Integrated Marketing. Sit alongside Integrated Marketing from the start of campaign planning, so creative is built into strategy rather than added at the end. Help turn campaign briefs into ideas that earn attention.
  • Creative team leadership. Lead, coach, and grow a small creative team across Copy and Video. Model the craft, help your team members develop into stronger creative thinkers, and build the bench for Cyera’s next stage of growth.
  • Brand stewardship. Act as a guardian of Cyera’s voice and identity across the company. Give partners across marketing, sales, and product the creative guardrails they need to move fast without losing consistency.

Requirements

QUALIFICATIONS

  • 10-12 years of creative experience, including time as an art director, creative director, or similar role, ideally at a B2B technology company or a category-defining brand.
  • A portfolio that proves the partnership between visual and copy. You can point to campaigns where the idea, the design, and the words worked as one.
  • Enterprise brand experience. You know how to make a serious, technical brand feel human and memorable without losing credibility.
  • Hands-on craft. You can sketch a concept, sharpen a headline, or direct a shoot yourself, not just brief someone else to do it.
  • AI fluency. You know how to define where and how AI tools fit into the creative process, using them to raise quality and velocity together rather than trading one for the other.
  • Strong stakeholder management. You build trust with partners across marketing, sales, and product, and you know how to hold a creative point of view while navigating competing priorities.
  • People leadership. You’ve hired, coached, and grown creative talent, and people want to do their best work for you.
  • Collaborative range. You work well with design, marketing, and brand strategy partners, and you know how to hold a creative point of view without slowing a team down.

This position is responsible for developing, implementing, and continuously improving process safety programs that protect employees, contractors, communities, company assets, and the environment while ensuring compliance with applicable European, local country, and company requirements.


The role provides technical leadership and governance for process safety management (PSM), risk assessment, management of change (MOC), major hazard prevention programs, fire and explosion prevention, hazardous materials management, emergency preparedness, and process safety performance improvement initiatives. The Process Safety Manager partners closely with Operations, Engineering, Maintenance, Quality, Supply Chain, Regulatory Affairs, and site leadership teams to identify, assess, and mitigate process safety risks.


As a key member of the global EHS organization, the Process Safety Manager ensures alignment with corporate process safety standards while supporting country-specific regulatory obligations including Seveso III Directive requirements and other European major accident prevention regulations. The position requires approximately 35% travel to support audits, risk assessments, incident investigations, project reviews, emergency preparedness exercises, and facility engagement activities across Europe.

  • Interface with regulatory agencies and support inspections, audits, permitting activities, and regulatory submissions.

Process Hazard Analysis & Risk Management

  • Lead and facilitate Process Hazard Analyses (PHA) utilizing methodologies such as HAZOP, What-If, FMEA, Layer of Protection Analysis (LOPA), and other recognized risk assessment techniques.
  • Ensure timely completion and revalidation of hazard assessments.
  • Develop risk reduction recommendations and monitor implementation of corrective actions.
  • Evaluate process safety risks associated with existing and new operations.

Management of Change (MOC)

  • Lead and oversee Management of Change processes for equipment, technology, process, organizational, and procedural changes.
  • Evaluate proposed modifications for process safety risks and compliance impacts.
  • Ensure appropriate technical review, approval, and documentation of changes.
  • Verify implementation of risk mitigation actions before startup.

Engineering & Capital Project Support

  • Provide process safety oversight for capital projects, facility expansions, equipment upgrades, and new process introductions.
  • Participate in design reviews, hazard evaluations, pre-startup safety reviews, and commissioning activities.
  • Ensure process safety requirements are incorporated into project design and execution.
  • Support safe integration of new technologies and operational processes.

Incident Investigation & Organizational Learning

  • Lead investigations of significant process safety incidents, near misses, fires, explosions, chemical releases, and high-potential events.
  • Apply structured root cause analysis methodologies to identify systemic causes.
  • Develop corrective and preventive actions and monitor effectiveness.
  • Share lessons learned across sites to strengthen organizational learning and risk reduction.

Fire, Explosion & Hazardous Materials Risk Management

  • Oversee programs related to combustible dusts, flammable liquids, reactive chemicals, compressed gases, and hazardous materials storage.
  • Evaluate facility safeguards related to fire prevention, explosion protection, loss prevention, and emergency response.
  • Support process safety requirements related to chemical handling, storage, segregation, and transportation.

Audit, Assurance & Continuous Improvement

  • Develop and execute process safety audit programs for European facilities.
  • Conduct site assessments to verify compliance with corporate and regulatory requirements.
  • Track audit findings and facilitate closure of corrective actions.
  • Benchmark industry best practices and recommend opportunities for performance improvement.

Mechanical Integrity & Operational Excellence

  • Support development and oversight of mechanical integrity programs for critical process equipment.
  • Collaborate with Maintenance and Engineering teams to improve asset reliability and risk management.
  • Review inspection, testing, preventive maintenance, and integrity management practices.
  • Monitor performance indicators to identify emerging risks and opportunities.

Training & Workforce Development

  • Develop and deliver process safety training programs for employees, contractors, engineers, supervisors, and site leaders.
  • Coach facility teams on process safety principles, risk assessment methodologies, and regulatory requirements.
  • Serve as a technical resource for process safety-related questions and problem solving.

Emergency Preparedness & Business Continuity

  • Support emergency response planning and major incident preparedness activities.
  • Participate in emergency drills, exercises, and crisis management initiatives.
  • Evaluate emergency response capabilities related to hazardous material incidents and process upsets.
  • Assist facilities in strengthening resilience and business continuity planning.

QUALIFICATIONS (Education/Training, Experience and/or Certifications)

Education / Training

Required

  • Bachelor's degree in Chemical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Environmental Engineering, Process Engineering, Occupational Safety, or a related technical discipline.

Preferred

  • Master's degree in Engineering, Process Safety, Risk Management, Safety Management, or a related field.

Experience

Required

  • Minimum 8–10 years of progressive experience in process safety, EHS, engineering, manufacturing, chemical processing, pharmaceuticals, specialty materials, energy, or industrial operations.
  • Demonstrated experience developing, implementing, and managing Process Safety Management programs.
  • Experience facilitating Process Hazard Analyses and risk assessments.
  • Experience leading incident investigations and Management of Change programs.
  • Proven success working with cross-functional operational and engineering teams across multiple locations.

Preferred

  • Experience supporting European manufacturing operations.
  • Experience with Seveso-regulated facilities or major accident hazard programs.
  • Experience supporting capital projects, facility expansions, and new process introductions.
  • Experience working within multinational organizations.

Certifications

Preferred

  • Certified Process Safety Professional (CCPSC)
  • Certified Safety Professional (CSP)
  • Chartered Engineer (CEng) or equivalent engineering registration
  • NEBOSH Diploma or equivalent professional safety qualification
  • Functional Safety or Risk Management certification
  • OSHA 30-Hour General Industry Certification
  • Six Sigma Green Belt or Black Belt certification

KNOWLEDGE, SKILLS AND ABILITIES (Those necessary to perform the job competently)

  • Extensive knowledge of process safety principles, risk management systems, and major accident prevention programs.
  • Strong understanding of Seveso III Directive requirements and European process safety regulations.
  • Knowledge of OSHA PSM, EPA RMP, CCPS Risk-Based Process Safety principles, NFPA standards, and related industry frameworks.
  • Expertise in hazard identification and risk assessment methodologies including HAZOP, LOPA, FMEA, Bow-Tie Analysis, and What-If reviews.
  • Strong knowledge of Management of Change, Mechanical Integrity, Incident Investigation, and Emergency Response systems.
  • Ability to evaluate fire, explosion, chemical release, and process upset hazards.
  • Strong analytical, investigative, and problem-solving skills.
  • Excellent written, verbal, and presentation skills.
  • Ability to effectively influence leaders and stakeholders without direct authority.
  • Strong project management and organizational skills.
  • Ability to manage multiple priorities across geographically dispersed operations.
  • Skilled in technical report writing, performance metrics development, and audit management.
  • Proficient in Microsoft Office Suite and EHS management systems.
  • Ability to interpret complex technical and regulatory requirements and translate them into practical operational solutions.
  • Strong business acumen and decision-making capability in high-risk operational environments.

ENVIRONMENTAL WORKING CONDITIONS & PHYSICAL EFFORT (Under Typical Positions)

  • Environmental Working Conditions & Physical Effort
  • Position is primarily remote/home-office based with regular travel to manufacturing, distribution, laboratory, warehouse, and processing facilities throughout Europe.
  • Approximately 35% travel is required, including domestic and international travel, overnight stays, and occasional short-notice site visits.
  • Exposure to manufacturing and industrial environments involving chemicals, hazardous materials, machinery, elevated work platforms, confined spaces, construction activities, and process equipment.
  • Must be able to wear required personal protective equipment (PPE), including safety glasses, hard hats, hearing protection, safety footwear, and respiratory protection where required.
  • Frequent walking through industrial facilities, climbing stairs and ladders, and conducting field inspections.
  • Ability to lift and carry up to 25 pounds occasionally.
  • Ability to sit, stand, walk, bend, reach, and work on a computer for extended periods.
  • Must be capable of responding to emergency situations, participating in audits and investigations, and accessing operational areas as needed.
  • Ability to travel internationally and maintain flexibility to support business needs across multiple countries and time zones.

The Senior Data Architect, Research Analytics will lead the South Carolina Clinical and Translational Science (SCTR) Institute’s data and reporting strategy and will engage with enterprise IS data leadership and teams to strategize for the design, creation, refinement, and long-term sustainability of an enterprise research data repository that integrates and curates data from multiple disparate systems across the research lifecycle. This role serves as a critical technical and strategic partner to IS and research leadership and administration, finance, operations, compliance, and analytics teams.

The Senior Data Architect will lead the development of a trusted, scalable research data environment supporting SCTR’s metric tracking and reporting and continuous quality improvement data strategy and decision-making. The position will enable comprehensive reporting across financial performance, awards, earned revenue, operational efficiency, research performance, regulatory compliance, and study and participant-level metrics.

Job Description

Job Description:

The Senior Data Architect, Research Analytics will lead the South Carolina Clinical and Translational Science (SCTR) Institute’s data and reporting strategy and will engage with enterprise IS data leadership and teams to strategize for the design, creation, refinement, and long-term sustainability of an enterprise research data repository that integrates and curates' data from multiple disparate systems across the research lifecycle. This role serves as a critical technical and strategic partner to IS and research leadership and administration, finance, operations, compliance, and analytics teams.

The Senior Data Architect will lead the development of a trusted, scalable research data environment supporting SCTR’s metric tracking and reporting and continuous quality improvement data strategy and decision-making. The position will enable comprehensive reporting across financial performance, awards, earned revenue, operational efficiency, research performance, regulatory compliance, and study and participant-level metrics.


Job Duties:

Research Data Repository Architecture & Design 20%

  • Engage with enterprise IS Data teams to design and maintain the logical and physical architecture of a centralized research repository integrating data from numerous source systems, including but not limited to:
  • Financial systems (awards, expenditures, revenue, effort)
  • Grants and contracts management systems
  • Clinical trial management systems (CTMS)
  • Research service request systems (SPARC)
  • Institutional Review Board (IRB) and Compliance Systems
  • Learning management and training systems
  • Human resources and faculty appointment systems

Define standards for data modeling, normalization, dimensional modeling, and metadata management to ensure data quality, scalability, and performance


Data Integration & Curation 20%

  • Lead the development of robust ETL/ELT pipelines to ingest, harmonize, and curate data from disparate systems with varying structures, definitions, and data quality.
  • Ensure alignment between System APIs, and Integrations looking at workflows of systems such as RIMD, SPARC, CTMS, IRB, Epic, and financial systems.
  • Establish and document authoritative data sources, business rules, and transformation logic for research metrics.
  • Ensure consistent representation of investigators, departments, academic medical center (AMC) affiliations, colleges, and organizational hierarchies across systems.
  • Implement processes to manage historical data, changes to organizational structures, and longitudinal reporting. (Essential)

Research Metrics & Analytics Enablement 15%

  • Translate business requirements into data models and visualizations across key research domains, including:

o Financial performance (awards, expenditures, earned revenue, cost recovery)

o Research portfolio and award activity

o Operational performance and efficiency

o Research study activation timelines and cycle times

o Participant recruitment volumes, accrual rates, and demographic characteristics

o IRB approvals, protocol status, and regulatory timelines

o Required training and compliance approvals

  • Ensure the data mart supports reproducible, auditable research metrics used for internal and external reporting.

Continuous Quality Improvement (CQI) 15%

  • Partner with research operations and quality teams to enable data-driven continuous quality improvement initiatives.
  • Develop metrics and dashboards that identify process bottlenecks, variability, and opportunities for improvement across the research lifecycle.
  • Support longitudinal trend analysis and benchmarking to assess the impact of operational changes.

Leadership Reporting & Workforce Planning 10%

  • Support SCTR and research leadership and grant reporting by delivering reliable, interpretable data for strategic decision-making.
  • Enable analyses used to justify workforce hires, capacity needs, and resource allocation based on research volume, complexity, and performance indicators.
  • Ensure visualizations and KPIs are suitable for board-level, sponsor-facing, and regulatory reporting.

Data Governance, Quality & Security 10%

  • Collaborate with data governance bodies to define data ownership, stewardship, access controls, and usage standards and support evaluation requests for integrating new vendor promoted tools and technologies into existing infrastructure.
  • Implement data quality monitoring, validation, and remediation processes.

Ensure compliance with institutional policies and applicable regulations related to data privacy, security, and research compliance.


Stakeholder Collaboration & Communication 10%

  • Act as a technical liaison between SCTR, IT, research administration, clinical research teams, finance, and institutional leadership.
  • Translate complex technical concepts into clear, actionable insights for non-technical stakeholders.
  • Provide technical leadership and mentorship to analysts, data engineers, and reporting teams.

MUSC Minimum Training and Experience Requirements:

A bachelor's degree in computer science, information systems or a related field and four years’ experience in systems development and maintenance, technical support or the support of complex database management systems. Related experience may be substituted for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis.

Related experience may be substituted for the bachelor's degree on a year-for-year basis. Scope includes migration planning with zero SEO loss, a reusable component library, Core Web Vitals targets met before launch, full GTM and GA4 rebuilt cleanly, and schema implementation across the new site. After launch, you transition into ongoing ownership.

What you'll own

  • Website development. Building and maintaining our WordPress site, shipping new landing pages, location pages, and service pages on demand. Expected publishing cadence after launch: 3 to 5 new pages per week using the component library.
  • Page speed and Core Web Vitals. This is the heart of the role. LCP, INP, CLS, PageSpeed scores. Continuous monitoring, image optimization, script auditing, caching strategy. Slow pages are not acceptable.
  • Cloudflare and WP Engine. Cache rules, page rules, security settings, firewall configuration, staging environments, plugin audits, security updates. You own the platform, not just the pages.
  • Schema implementation. The SEO specialist defines schema strategy. You handle JSON-LD implementation, structured data testing, deployment, and validation across LocalBusiness, Service, FAQPage, Review, and BreadcrumbList types.
  • Analytics and attribution. GTM, GA4, conversion tracking across Google Ads, Bing, Facebook, Reddit, and WhatConverts. When tracking breaks, you diagnose and fix it. Attribution is a craft, not an afterthought.
  • Technical SEO foundation. Sitemaps, robots.txt, crawl budget, canonicals, 301 redirects, indexation issues, Search Console error resolution.
  • Conversion rate optimization. Continuous A/B testing on hero sections, forms, CTAs, and page layouts.
  • Mobile-first development and accessibility. Most of our customers convert on mobile. Every page is built mobile-first. WCAG 2.1 AA compliance expected.

How you work with the team

You'll partner closely with our Senior SEO Specialist. They own the strategy (content, link building, schema specs, internal linking strategy). You own the technical surface that brings it to life. Daily Slack collaboration, weekly working session, clean handoff process.

You'll also have a weekly working session with our CMO and direct access to the founder. No agency layer. No buried management chain.

What you need to have

  • 5+ years of hands-on web development experience. You've shipped real work and you can prove it.
  • Deep WordPress and Elementor Pro fluency. You build in Elementor every day and know its limits.
  • PHP fluency. You can write custom functions, build custom post types, and modify themes when Elementor isn't enough.
  • Real Cloudflare and WP Engine experience. You've configured cache rules, firewalls, staging environments, and managed production sites end to end.
  • Real attribution and analytics chops. GTM, GA4, conversion tracking across multiple ad platforms. You can debug a broken pixel.
  • Schema implementation expertise. JSON-LD, structured data testing, the technical knowledge to deploy and validate.
  • Page speed obsession. You can walk us through specific optimizations you made and the before/after metrics that resulted.
  • Site migration experience. You've led at least one full WordPress rebuild without losing rankings, conversions, or tracked attribution.
  • Home services or local business website experience. This is a must. We want people who've shaped real local businesses, not Fortune 500 division work.
  • Strong written English and Pacific Time Zone hours. We're not interested in candidates who plan to flip their schedule for this role.

A note on how we work

This is a 100% remote role. We don't use monitoring software and we don't micromanage. We trust our team to do excellent work and communicate proactively. That trust runs both ways. Show up, take ownership, operate with high integrity.

This role is full-time. Not a side gig. Your full attention during business hours is part of what we're paying for.

jobs.description:
Are you a graduate keen on data and looking for a chance to kickstart your career? Rockborne could be the place for you with our Data Programme!

Our mission is to grow, develop and deploy the world’s leading data professionals, make real change in the data industry through the diversity of thought and keep quality at the heart of everything we do.

The Programme

Our Academy is a 12-week free online training programme that is designed and delivered by our dedicated in-house team of data gurus and industry legends. We focus on all elements of Data from Data Analytics to Data Science and more, whilst also putting huge emphasis on communication and professional skills.
The curriculum is like no other, it is packed full of everything we know the data industry and our clients need. You’ll be taken through a carefully curated training programme that covers Excel, SQL, PowerBI, Tableau, Python, Data Governance, GenAI, Presentation skills, Stakeholder Management and more. On completing the Academy you’ll commence to the next stage in your learning and development and join us on Advance!
Advance is where you’ll take your data and AI skills to the next level through various projects and sprints. This additional 12 weeks of development is the real game changer, being designed to enhance and hone your newly found data and AI skills. This will take you from data novice to a data ninja – having every tool at your disposal to tackle data and AI challenges and bring real value. During the Advance period we will organise interviews with our clients across the data industry and aim for you to join us as a Rockborne employee and become a Data Consultant with one of our clients for the next two years, this would be your Assignment!
Assignments are across the UK but are mainly focused in London and are with a broad and diverse client group, from financial services to aviation to pharmaceutical. When you commence an assignment you’ll become a Rockborne employee and receive a salary which increases over the two years. Not only that, you’ll also continue to receive dedicated support from the team at Rockborne with regular 121s, mentoring and tailor made training plans that align to you and your assignment.
At the end of an Assignment, there will be the potential to transition to the client company, taking a permanent role and next step in your career. If you're interested in exploring other options, we can support in identifying your next role through our sister company Harnham, one of the largest Data and AI recruitment agencies globally. You’ll also become part of our Alumni network, providing the latest data insights and trends, regular events and updates and access to a wide network of colleagues and peers across the data realm.
We may not be able to provide everyone with an assignment through our clients but by completing our Academy and Advance programmes you will now have a wealth of training and experience to take to the job market. It’s completely free training, there is never anything to pay back and we will try our hardest to support you in finding your next role through either Rockborne or externally.

Skills, Knowledge and Experience

Your Skills & Experience
· Educated to a degree level with a strong interest in data - you don't need set grades or a certain degree to join us
· A natural problem solver, comfortable translating complex issues in a clear and easy to understand way
· A self-starter who is willing to go the extra mile either for your client’s benefit, or building your own knowledge agenda
· A desire to work in a stakeholder focused environment, comfortable blending the technical with a more client-facing aspect

Application

· Submit your profile via the ‘Apply now’ button
· Your CV will be reviewed by a real person
· Telephone interview - an introduction call to Rockborne, you interview us!
· Online numerical test - coming into data, numbers are important and that's all we are looking at
· Video call - asking you to undertake some research for us in data, can you showcase what you've learnt
And that's it, no psychometrics, trip hazards or bots.
We would love to hear from you and learn more about you and you personal goals and drivers.

Job Summary

Principal Threat Intelligence Hunter - Unit 42 Managed Threat Hunting

Job Description Summary

The Principal Threat Intelligence Hunter will sit within Unit 42 Managed Threat Hunting and support proactive, intelligence-led hunting across customer environments. This role combines hands-on threat hunting with cyber threat intelligence analysis, helping multinational organizations stay one step ahead of adversaries and cyber threats.

The Cyber Threat Intelligence Hunter will analyze public and private threat intelligence, Unit 42 research, adversary campaigns, malware activity, infrastructure, indicators, and TTPs, then translate that intelligence into actionable hunting hypotheses, investigation workflows, hunting queries, and customer-facing findings.

This role will work across large-scale customer telemetry to investigate suspicious activity, validate emerging threats, support scheduled hunts, and contribute to timely, professional reporting. The role will also collaborate closely with threat hunters, detection engineers, incident responders, MDR teams, and Unit 42 intelligence and security researchers to operationalize intelligence quickly and improve hunting outcomes across the service.

This is a proactive, research-driven hunting role for someone who can connect external intelligence with real-world telemetry, understand and fingerprint attacker behavior, investigate security data, and clearly communicate findings to both technical and non-technical audiences.

Your Impact

Help multinational organizations stay one step ahead of adversaries and cyber threats.

Serve as a key contributor within Unit 42 Managed Threat Hunting, combining hands-on threat hunting execution with cyber threat intelligence analysis.

Analyze public and private threat intelligence, Unit 42 research, adversary campaigns, malware activity, infrastructure, indicators, and TTPs.

Translate threat intelligence into actionable hunting hypotheses, investigation workflows, hunting queries, and customer-facing findings.

Execute existing threat hunting reports and hunting workflows, investigate results, and support timely customer reporting.

Investigate scheduled hunt detections and compose clear, professional reports when relevant.

Investigate hunting leads based on IOCs, threat intelligence, internal detections, customer telemetry, and emerging adversary behaviors.

Monitor the threat landscape and prepare initial context for emerging campaigns, enabling the global team to continue deeper investigation and hunting.

Collaborate with threat hunters, detection engineers, incident responders, MDR, and Unit 42 researchers to operationalize intelligence quickly and effectively.

Escalate major, unclear, or high-impact security events to the Threat Hunting leadership team when necessary.

Provide ongoing feedback on findings, hunting reports, queries, intelligence workflows, and operational processes to support continuous improvement.

Contribute to making the world a safer and better place.

Why Choose Us

Perform meaningful, intelligence-led threat hunting across a wide variety of data sources.

Gain hands-on experience translating emerging threat intelligence into real hunting outcomes across customer environments.

Work across multiple cybersecurity domains, including endpoint, network, cloud, identity, and third-party vendor telemetry.

Learn how threat intelligence is converted into hypotheses, queries, investigations, validations, and customer-facing reports.

Join a global team of experts who handle threats and adversaries at scale every day.

Collaborate closely with Unit 42 researchers, incident responders, detection engineers, MDR teams, and experienced threat hunters.

Help improve how threat intelligence is operationalized across a managed service.

Take part in the continuous improvement of hunting reports, queries, workflows, automation, AI-driven hunting capabilities, and operational processes.

We believe in automation, AI, intelligence-led hunting, and scalable security outcomes.

Qualifications

Your Experience

  • 6+ years of experience in tactical threat hunting, cyber threat intelligence (CTI), DFIR, or advanced security operations.
  • Strong background in tactical threat intelligence, specifically identifying the discrete traces, artifacts, and behavioral fingerprints left by adversaries across diverse telemetry sources (endpoint, network, cloud, and identity).
  • Experience capturing and modelling incident data to map out intrusions and understand attacker behaviours.
  • Proven ability to develop & deliver verbal & written technical findings of attacker behaviour into clear, high-impact notifications for customers.
  • Experience translating threat intelligence into high-fidelity hunting hypotheses, detection logic, and log-based queries.
  • Bonus Points: Experience in an Incident Response or Managed Services environment, proficiency in Python and SQL, or familiarity with malware analysis, published security blogs or research that shows a deep understanding of a particular threat.

The Team

We’re not your ordinary Threat Hunting team. We’re a diverse and global group of security professionals who deal with big data, emerging threats, adversary behavior, threat intelligence, and customer telemetry in order to remain one step ahead of attackers.

Being a Cyber Threat Intelligence Hunter within Unit 42 Managed Threat Hunting is an opportunity to sit at the intersection of threat intelligence, proactive hunting, detection logic, incident response insights, and customer-facing security outcomes. You’ll work with some of the brightest minds in cybersecurity and help turn intelligence into action at global scale.

We are looking for an experienced and highly adaptable Construction Project Manager to coordinate projects, trades, suppliers, logistics, and day-to-day operational requirements.

Construction project management experience is the number-one priority for this hire. The successful candidate should understand how construction projects operate in practice: coordinating multiple trades, chasing deadlines, solving unexpected problems, managing dependencies, and ensuring work continues progressing.

This is deliberately a broad role rather than a narrowly defined Project Manager position. We are a growing business where processes and SOPs are still being developed, so you will regularly be asked to step outside traditional project management responsibilities and assist with research, administration, executive support, and other business priorities.

The right person will enjoy that variety and be comfortable being asked, “Can you figure this out?” even when there is not an established process to follow.

Construction Project Management – Primary Focus

  • Coordinate projects from planning through to completion
  • Manage project schedules, timelines, milestones, and outstanding actions
  • Coordinate trades, contractors, suppliers, and other project stakeholders
  • Proactively chase trades and suppliers to ensure agreed deadlines are met
  • Identify project delays, dependencies, and potential risks before they become larger problems
  • Coordinate materials, equipment, and site requirements
  • Maintain visibility across multiple moving parts and competing priorities
  • Keep management informed of project progress, delays, and required decisions
  • Maintain accurate project information, tasks, and documentation
  • Help establish stronger project management processes as the business grows

Trade & Supplier Coordination

A significant component of this role will involve direct phone communication with Australian trades, suppliers, local government and other regulators, as well as with the internal team.

Responsibilities will include:

  • Contact trades and suppliers to confirm availability, pricing, and timelines
  • Follow up overdue work, materials, and outstanding commitments
  • Accountability with stakeholders for clear answers and realistic delivery dates
  • Coordinate information between different trades and project stakeholders
  • Source alternative suppliers or contractors when existing options are unavailable
  • Maintain professional relationships while being sufficiently assertive to keep projects moving
  • Regular and ongoing communication with key team members regarding status and progress of projects and key tasks.

The successful candidate must be confident on the phone and comfortable having direct conversations when deadlines are at risk.

Research & Problem Solving

  • Independently research solutions to unusual project and operational requirements
  • Source suppliers, contractors, products, and specialist services in Australia
  • Research requirements for regional and remote Australian councils, policies and regulations
  • Find practical solutions for logistics such as crane operators, transport providers, specialist trades, materials, or staircase designs
  • Compare suppliers, pricing, specifications, and availability
  • Work through large amounts of information and identify the most practical solution
  • Use AI and online research tools to accelerate research while independently validating information
  • Present management with clear options and recommendations rather than simply forwarding raw information

Project Documentation & Systems

  • Maintain accurate project records and documentation
  • Track actions, deadlines, milestones, and outstanding requirements
  • Maintain project information within the company’s chosen project management system
  • Organise supplier quotes, contracts, drawings, and supporting documentation
  • Assist with developing project templates, checklists, and workflows
  • Support document processes by contributing to SOPs as repeatable workflows emerge
  • Create greater visibility and structure across projects without requiring established processes

General Operations & Administration

This role requires someone willing to support the wider business wherever needed, including:

  • General business administration
  • Preparing and organising documents
  • Maintaining spreadsheets and trackers
  • Following up emails and outstanding actions
  • Scheduling and meeting coordination
  • Supplier and contractor administration
  • Data entry and information management
  • Basic reporting and project updates
  • Assisting with Xero or basic financial administration where required
  • Supporting other operational priorities as they arise

Xero/bookkeeping capability is advantageous but is a low priority compared with construction project management and communication skills.

Executive & Personal Support

As part of the broad nature of the role, the successful candidate must also be comfortable assisting leadership with occasional EA and personal tasks.

This may include:

  • Research and information gathering
  • Scheduling and coordination
  • Following up external parties
  • Making bookings or arrangements

Why Mozilla?

Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. We make pioneering brands like Firefox, the privacy-minded web browser. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people.

The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms.

About this team and role:

Mozilla’s Customer Experience team helps users, organizations, and partners successfully adopt, use, and get sustained value from Mozilla products. Historically, much of Mozilla’s support work has focused on consumers. As Mozilla expands its business and organizational offerings, we are building a support operation designed for the needs of B2B customers, including dependable service delivery, clear customer commitments, global coverage, and close coordination with Product and Engineering.

As Staff Enterprise Support Operations Manager, you will be Mozilla’s first dedicated B2B support operations leader. You will not inherit a mature operation; you will build one. You will design and launch the operating model, vendor strategy, processes, tooling, training, metrics, capacity planning, and governance required to provide high-quality technical support to organizations deploying and managing Mozilla products.

Beyond building the support operation, you will serve as the operational bridge between Enterprise customers, CX, Product, and Engineering, ensuring insights from customers and support teams inform the broader Enterprise experience.

This is an individual contributor role with broad end-to-end ownership. You will be the day-to-day owner of Mozilla’s external B2B support vendor relationships and the operational processes connecting vendor agents with Mozilla teams. You will use customer demand, service performance, and cost data to determine when and how the operation should expand across geographies, languages, coverage models, and support offerings. As the business grows, you will also help define the structure and capabilities of Mozilla’s future B2B support team.

You will participate in a defined incident coverage model and periodically lead the operational response to major customer incidents. In those moments, you will ensure vendors follow established procedures, coordinate escalation and handoffs to Mozilla engineers, drive cross-functional resolution, communicate clearly with customers and internal leaders, and oversee post-incident reviews and root cause analysis.

This position requires a rare combination of support operations expertise, vendor management, program development, technical fluency, and calm leadership under pressure. Our ideal candidate is a practical builder who can move between strategy and execution, create structure where none exists, and earn the trust of customers, vendors, engineers, and senior leaders.

What you’ll do:
  • Build and launch Mozilla’s first B2B support operations capability, including its operating model, workflows, escalation paths, governance, and continuous-improvement processes.
  • Own external support vendor relationships end to end, including future vendor selection and contracting support, onboarding, workforce planning, performance management, invoicing, renewals, and investment recommendations.
  • Create and maintain vendor training, support playbooks, standard operating procedures, quality frameworks, knowledge materials, and coordination with product teams for release-readiness plans.
  • Forecast customer demand and support capacity, balancing staffing, coverage, language needs, service quality, cost, and business growth; recommend when to expand into new geographies or service models.
  • Define service objectives, metrics, KPIs, dashboards, and operating reviews for quality, speed, customer experience, productivity, and cost.
  • Hold vendors accountable for performance, identify service gaps, and lead corrective-action and continuous-improvement plans.
  • Own Mozilla’s operational enterprise escalation framework while designing and managing operational handoffs between vendor agents and Mozilla teams so complex issues reach the right Engineering, Product, Security, or business partners with sufficient context and urgency.
  • Lead the operational response to major B2B incidents, coordinating vendor execution, engineering engagement, customer and leadership communications, resolution, and post-incident review.
  • Partner with Product, Engineering, Customer Success, Sales, Legal, Finance, Procurement, and other teams to align customer commitments with operational capacity and improve the support experience.
  • Participate in customer-facing meetings to understand operational challenges, explain support processes, gather feedback, and strengthen the customer support experience.
  • Translate support trends and customer feedback into actionable insights, partnering cross-functionally to improve customer journeys, products, documentation, processes, tooling, automation, and responsible uses of AI, while helping define the future structure of Mozilla’s B2B support organization.
What you’ll bring:
  • 5+ years of experience in B2B or enterprise technical support operations, service delivery, customer operations, vendor management, or a related field.
  • Demonstrated experience building a new support capability or substantially scaling or transforming an existing support operation.
  • Experience managing outsourced support vendors or BPO partners, including training, workforce planning, quality assurance, performance governance, and corrective action.
  • Experience with vendor selection, statements of work, contracts, budgets, forecasts, invoices, renewals, or related procurement and commercial processes.
  • Experience with support platforms such as Zendesk/CRMs and issue-tracking systems such as Jira, including reporting, workflow design, and operational analytics.
  • Strong knowledge of enterprise support and service-management practices, including service levels, severity models, escalations, incident management, problem management, and root cause analysis.
  • Experience leading high-severity technical incidents and coordinating customers, support teams, engineers, executives, and other stakeholders under pressure.
  • Experience defining operational metrics and using dashboards, reporting, and workforce planning to improve quality, customer outcomes, efficiency, and cost.
  • Technical fluency sufficient to coordinate issues involving enterprise software, browsers, endpoint management, identity, certificates, proxies, networks, security tools, and managed customer environments; deep software engineering expertise is not required.
  • Excellent communication and cross-functional leadership skills, with the ability to explain complex situations clearly and move work forward across distributed teams.
  • Ability to operate independently across regions, cultures, and time zones, exercise sound judgment in ambiguous situations, and build support experiences worthy of long-term customer trust.
  • Experience with multilingual or multi-region support operations is desired.
  • Experience building and leading B2B or enterprise technical support operations teams is desired.
  • Familiarity with GDPR, enterprise security requirements, regulated customer environments is desired.
What you’ll get:
  • Generous performance-based bonus plans to all eligible employees - we share in our success as one team
  • Rich medical, dental, and vision coverage
  • Generous retirement contributions with 100% immediate vesting (regardless of whether you contribute)
  • Quarterly all-company wellness days where everyone takes a pause together
  • Country specific holidays plus a day off for your birthday
  • One-time home office stipend
  • Annual professional development budget
  • Quarterly well-being stipend
  • Considerable paid parental leave
  • Employee referral bonus program
  • Other benefits (life/AD&D, disability, EAP, etc. - varies by country)

About Mozilla

Mozilla exists to build the Internet as a public resource accessible to all because we believe that open and free is better than closed and controlled. When you work at Mozilla, you give yourself a chance to make a difference in the lives of Web users everywhere. And you give us a chance to make a difference in your life every single day. Join us to work on the Web as the platform and help create more opportunity and innovation for everyone online.

Commitment to diversity, equity, inclusion, and belonging

Mozilla understands that valuing diverse creative practices and forms of knowledge are crucial to and enrich the company’s core mission. We encourage applications from everyone, including members of all equity-seeking communities, such as (but certainly not limited to) women, racialized and Indigenous persons, persons with disabilities, persons of all sexual orientations, gender identities, and expressions.

  • Experience in being professionally edited for publication.

  • Experience in using WordPress for content creation.
  • Experience with the Slack communication app.

Abilities Required

  • Internet access and use.

Who is Bionews?
Bionews is a leading online health, science, publication, and research company with one purpose: to serve patients with a rare or chronic disease. We do this by connecting them with current, trusted, and relevant news and information. This content is delivered regularly and provided by actual patients as well as professional journalists, writers, editors, scientists, and experienced media executives. Our end customers are truly patients living with rare and chronic diseases. Visit www.bionews.com for more information.

To empower, inspire, and champion the patient voice as the preeminent resource that engages, informs, and connects the global rare and chronic disease community.

jobs.excerpt: Stell dir vor:Du rufst jemanden an.  Er hebt ab.  Nicht genervt — erleichtert.
jobs.description:
Stell dir vor:

Du rufst jemanden an. Er hebt ab. Nicht genervt — erleichtert. Weil du genau in dem Moment anrufst, in dem er selbst gerade überlegt, ob es eine Lösung für sein Problem gibt.

Kein Zufall. Kein Glück. Daten.

Genau das ist timedleads.

Unsere Geschichte:

Jeder Vertriebler kennt das Gefühl: Du arbeitest dich durch hunderte Kontakte, schreibst perfekte E-Mails, trainierst deinen Pitch — und trotzdem landet die Hälfte im Papierkorb. Nicht weil du schlecht bist. Sondern weil das Timing falsch war.

Wir haben uns gefragt: Was wäre, wenn man genau weiß, wann jemand kaufbereit ist?

Die Antwort ist timedleads. Wir analysieren Trigger-Ereignisse — Firmenumzüge, Neueinstellungen, Finanzierungsrunden, Technologiewechsel — und liefern unseren Kunden monatlich strukturierte Lead-Listen genau der Unternehmen, bei denen gerade etwas passiert. Kein Rauschen. Nur Signal.

Wir stehen am Anfang. Und wir suchen jemanden, der mit uns die Kategorie definiert.

Aufgaben

  • Entwicklung und Umsetzung von B2B-Outbound-Strategien zur Identifikation neuer Geschäftsmöglichkeiten unter Verwendung unserer einzigartigen Trigger-basierten Timing-Leads.
  • Aufbau und Pflege nachhaltiger Beziehungen zu Entscheidungsträgern in potenziellen Kundenunternehmen durch gezielte und zeitlich abgestimmte Kontaktaufnahme.
  • Durchführung von Verkaufsgesprächen und Verhandlungen, um den Nutzen und die Vorteile unserer Dienstleistungen überzeugend darzustellen und Geschäftsabschlüsse zu sichern.
  • Analyse von Markttrends und Kundenanforderungen, um maßgeschneiderte Lösungen anzubieten und den Verkaufsprozess kontinuierlich zu optimieren.
  • Enge Zusammenarbeit mit dem internen Team, um Feedback aus Kundengesprächen zu teilen und die Weiterentwicklung unserer Dienstleistungen voranzutreiben.

Qualifikation

Was wir suchen:

Keinen Lebensläufe-Optimierer. Keinen Konferenztisch-Nickerchen-Experten.

Wir suchen jemanden, der morgens aufwacht und Bock hat. Der Ablehnung als Feedback versteht, nicht als Niederlage. Der einen Deal abschließt und direkt den nächsten angehen will.

Du hast Erfahrung im B2B-Vertrieb. Du weißt, wie man eine Pipeline aufbaut. Du willst nicht verwaltet werden — du willst gestalten.

Dann bist du hier richtig.

Benefits

Was wir dir anbieten — ehrlich und direkt:

  • Vergütung ohne Deckel: 10.000 € bis 200.000 € / Jahr — je nachdem, was du draus machst
  • 100 % Remote, keine Kernzeiten, keine Bürokratie
  • Direkter Zugang zum Gründer — kein Mittelsmann, keine Politik
  • Du bist nicht Mitarbeiter Nummer 47. Du bist der erste Vertriebler. Dein Fingerabdruck bleibt.

„Ich habe timedleads gegründet, weil ich es satt hatte zuzusehen, wie brillante Vertriebler gegen eine Wand aus schlechtem Timing laufen. Der beste Pitch der Welt scheitert, wenn er zur falschen Zeit kommt. Das wollte ich ändern — und jetzt suche ich jemanden, der genauso brennt wie ich."

— Gründer

Bist du dabei?

Dann bewirb dich jetzt. Nicht irgendwann. Jetzt! - bevor jemand anderes diese Chance ergreift.

ID360 is a rapidly growing resilience and energy consulting firm committed to advancing smart building practices and energy efficiency. As part of our mission, we are seeking one or more experienced Heat Pump Water Heater (HPWH) Trainers for Municipal Facilities Staff on a contract basis position. This role will focus on training professionals on the maintenance and operations of heat pump equipment for public buildings.

Contract Opportunity:

We are seeking one or more experienced Heat Pump Water Heater to design and deliver hands-on, practical training for municipal facilities staff across the Bay Area. This is a contract-based engagement ideal for a seasoned Heat Pump Water Heater professional who is knowledgeable about heat pump technology and is comfortable training others virtually and in-person.

Facilities teams need practical, real-world knowledge to confidently operate and maintain modern heat pump systems and you’ll play a training role in building that capacity.

Role Details:
  • Location: Primarily virtual role with a limited in-person training delivery in the Bay Area
  • Compensation: Competitive hourly

Requirements

Key Responsibilities:
You will develop and facilitate training sessions focused on the operation and maintenance (O&M) of Heat Pump Water Heater (HPWH) systems installed in municipal facilities. Specific responsibilities include:
  • Designing curriculum tailored to the needs of facilities staff working in public buildings such as libraries, community centers, office buildings, and public safety facilities
  • Delivering engaging training sessions that build real operational confidence—not just theoretical knowledge
  • Covering topics such as day-to-day operations, preventative maintenance, controls integration, load management, and key differences from conventional gas-based systems

Qualifications:

  • Training & Communication Skills- Comfortable designing instructional content and leading sessions for working professionals, including:

    • Facilitating group training sessions in a way that engages participants and invites questions
  • Beyond equipment familiarity, strong candidates will demonstrate a solid understanding of how heat pump water heating systems differ from conventional gas or electric resistance systems, including:
    • Load shifting and demand management strategies
    • System sizing and performance considerations (e.g., climate, usage patterns)
    • Controls integration and commissioning best practices
    • Maintenance requirements and common troubleshooting scenarios
    • Energy efficiency and decarbonization benefits
We are especially interested in candidates who can draw from real-world field experience and translate that into engaging, practical training whether through workshops, demonstrations, or instructional materials for contractors, facility staff, or building professionals.

Job Description:

1. GENERAL POSITION INFORMATION

Position Name: Adjunct Faculty, Dissertation Chair – Sport and Performance Psychology (Online/Remote)

Classification: Part-time Adjunct

FTE: up to 18 hours per week

Work Hours: Variable due to online nature of program. Generally, 9a-3p PST M-F; may include evenings or weekends.

Department/Division: College of Graduate Studies

Supervisor: Director, Sport and Performance Psychology program

2.POSITION SUMMARY

University of Western States (UWS) is seeking adjunct faculty members within the department of Sport and Performance Psychology to serve as doctoral dissertation chairs.

Dissertation Chairs are responsible for supervising doctoral (EdD) candidates in designing and conducting a substantial individual research project required for completion of the doctoral degree in sport and performance psychology. Chairs will work closely with candidates to cultivate topic ideas, design appropriate methodology, secure approval by the Institutional Review Board (IRB), collect and analyze data, and submit the final work both to the university and to a selected professional outlet for publication. In addition, Dissertation Chairs will serve as the head of a 4-5 member Dissertation Committee, ensuring committee members’ timely review and feedback on candidate progress.

3.KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Provide an average of 3 hrs/week of support to each dissertation candidate supervised. That work will include, but is not limited to, the following activities (100%):

1. Adherence to the policies and procedures detailed in the UWS Dissertation Handbook

2. Mandatory use of the Canvas learning management system to document student work and chair feedback/guidance

3. Weekly product review and Zoom meetings with doctoral candidate

4. Attend and facilitate proposal defense and final defense via Zoom

5. Engage in regular communication with committee members

6. Participate in 1-2 individual meetings/term with Dissertation Coordinator

7. Attendance at, or review of recordings from, quarterly group meetings with dissertation faculty

4. UWS CORE VALUES AND ASSOCIATED COMPETENCIES
The following Core Values are integral to working at UWS. All employees, regardless of their position within the university, are expected uphold the Core Values and demonstrate associated competencies.

Best Practices: We maintain high standards by using and integrating evidence across multiple disciplines.

Curiosity: We are innovative, open minded, and forward thinking.

Inclusiveness: We are respectful, mindful, and welcoming of different ways of being, thinking, and doing.

Professionalism: We are responsible, respectful, and accountable.

Student-Focus: We work for the common good of students’ academic and professional success.

Whole-Person Health: We promote physical, mental and emotional wellness in all facets of the UWS experience.

5. POSITION QUALIFICATIONS

Required

Education & Training

  • Doctoral degree (e.g., PhD, EdD, PsyD) in sport and performance psychology, clinical mental health counseling, sport science, health science, or related field
  • Evidence of completed research

Memberships, Certifications & Licenses

  • Current membership and participation in appropriate state, regional, and national professional organizations appropriate to SPP

Experience

  • Evidence of publication, presentation, and continuing education in sport and performance psychology and/or clinical counseling

Related Knowledge, Skills, & Abilities

  • Proficiency with data analysis software (qualitative and/or qualitative)
  • Self-sufficiency in the management of personal schedule.
  • Proficient in document/report preparation adhering to institutional editorial guidelines.
  • Intermediate-to-advanced computer skills required (MS Office Outlook, Word, Excel, SharePoint, Adobe Acrobat Professional).
  • Proficiency with video conferencing systems.
  • Working understanding and experience with Canvas (or equivalent) learning management system.

Other Qualifications

  • Professional interpersonal skills including effective verbal and written communication.
  • Effective management of faculty and students in professional degree programs.
  • Demonstrated commitment to collegiality and shared governance.
  • Strong organizational skills and ability to prioritize/execute plans and resource management to achieve desired teaching outcomes.
  • Ability to work independently with minimal supervision.
  • Ability to exercise professional judgment and assume responsibility in clinical decision-making.
  • Ability to adapt quickly to a changing environment and learn new systems and processes.
  • Willingness and ability to follow direction from director, dean, administrators as consistent with university policy.
  • Working knowledge of FERPA student privacy regulations.

Preferred

Memberships, Certifications & Licenses

  • Current Certified Mental Performance Consultant (CMPC), AASP and/or
  • Current licensure in clinical mental health

Experience

  • Listed as first author for a research study published in a peer-reviewed journal
  • Evidence of prior service as a dissertation chair or committee member
  • Evidence of guiding student researchers through the process of peer-reviewed publication
  • Evidence of an ongoing research agenda

6. APPLICATION, SCREENING AND HIRING PROCESS:

Screening of applicants will begin immediately, and the position will remain open until filled. Please submit a cover letter and curriculum vitae. You may attach your materials as Word or PDF documents.

Official transcripts from prior institutions of higher learning must be received prior to offer being extended to the finalist.

University of Western States conducts background checks for the finalist or finalists of staff and faculty positions. The type of background check will vary by position type.

Endpoints News is seeking a newsbreaking policy reporter to cover the Food and Drug Administration.

How the biopharmaceutical industry is regulated has changed dramatically. There’s global pressure to move faster on trials, and the FDA is contending with changing consumer interest in compounding pharmacies that blur the lines between pharmaceuticals and wellness. What the FDA does next will be this reporter’s job to chronicle.

The right reporter will put regulations in context, scoop news on people and policy, and illuminate the push and pull between industry and government. Strong candidates will have a vision for the beat, an understanding of Endpoints’ mission and ambition, and a collaborative, team-first attitude.

Sans être exhaustifs, voici les services et livrables que devra fournir la personne retenue.

Description des travaux ou des biens livrables :

1- Accomplir diverses tâches de secrétariat requises par le chef de service et le personnel du service :
• Assurer l’ouverture et le suivi des dossiers d’aide financière;
• Assurer la numérisation de différents documents;
• Accompagner les agents de bureau de la direction dans leurs tâches;
• Assurer la préparation de divers documents;
• Effectuer le classement et faire des photocopies de divers documents;
• Effectuer l’archivage des dossiers électronique ou papier;
• Distribuer les télécopies reçues au personnel.
2- Participer à la préparation du déploiement du personnel à la suite d’un sinistre :
• Préparer les documents et le matériel nécessaires au déploiement du personnel du service;
• Apporter le soutien requis au personnel lors de la tenue de séances d’information publiques et lors des rencontres individuelles avec des sinistrés (installer le matériel dans la salle, accueillir les sinistrés, prendre des rendez-vous, photocopier des documents, etc.);
• Classer des documents.
3- Au besoin, remplacer les autres agents de bureau du service et le réceptionniste de la direction

Profil

• Détenir un diplôme d’études secondaires (DES);
• Avoir un grand souci du détail et faire preuve de rigueur ;
• Détenir les aptitudes à travailler en équipe ;
• De solides compétences de service à la clientèle et une forte capacité à entretenir de bonnes relations professionnelles avec ses collègues.

LIEU DE TRAVAIL

Le lieu de travail sera déterminé selon le mandat, il peut être en télétravail ou chez le client.

POURQUOI SE JOINDRE À TEHORA?

TEHORA est une firme québécoise multidisciplinaire reconnue pour l'excellence de ses services professionnels, de nature technique et de gestion de projets à l'échelle nationale et internationale. Notre mission est d'accompagner nos clients dans la concrétisation de leurs projets par l'excellence de notre savoir-faire et de notre créativité.

Depuis sa création en 2017, notre équipe de professionnels connait une croissance exponentielle en répondant aux besoins importants en gestion de

projets multidisciplinaires, dans le domaine des transports, du génie civil, du TI et plus.

Nos collaborateurs travaillent sur des mandats aussi bien à l’interne que chez des clients d’envergures.

TEHORA se distingue par sa culture d’entreprise, axée sur le bonheur de ses employés et la diversité.

Chez TEHORA, chaque collaborateur est un membre important de l'équipe qui contribue à notre succès collectif. Nos membres ont la flexibilité requise pour avoir un équilibre entre le travail et leur vie privée, tout en menant une carrière enrichissante.

Nous offrons un environnement de travail motivant. La diversité des projets, la grande autonomie et l’interaction directe avec les clients sont appréciées. Une telle proximité est possible en raison de notre structure organisationnelle horizontale, qui se traduit par des relations de confiance et une communication efficace entre notre équipe et les clients.

AVANTAGES
